before.story: California Governor Gavin Newsom Commutes State's 548 Death Row Sentences
before.summary: In one of his final executive acts before concluding his eight-year tenure, California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole. before.story: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse in Antalya Without Deal

before.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo, the world's largest cobalt producer, announced it will reimpose an export ban on the battery metal—the second supply cutoff in two years—to reverse falling global market prices.

after.story: DR Congo Reimposes Cobalt Export Ban to Shore Up Prices
after.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced a total suspension of cobalt exports starting November 30 to combat depressed global market prices. The announcement triggered a surge in Chinese cobalt stock valuations as battery material processors rush to secure shipments before the cutoff.

note: Chinese cobalt processing firms jump on stock market while racing to beat export deadline.

before.story: Malaysia's Anwar Says US Chip Curbs Won't Hurt China Ties
before.summary: Speaking in Shenzhen ahead of a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said U.S. AI chip restrictions will not affect Malaysia's ties with China, adding that Beijing has been easier to deal with than Washington amid superpower tech rivalry.

after.story: Malaysia's Anwar Says US Chip Curbs Won't Hurt China Ties
after.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim stated in Shenzhen that U.S. chip restrictions will not alter Malaysia's close diplomatic relationship with China. However, tech analysts warn that expanded Washington export licensing requirements could slow Malaysia's domestic AI data center construction boom.

note: U.S. semiconductor curbs threaten Malaysia's multi-billion dollar AI data center expansion.

before.story: Japan's Takaichi Faces Diplomatic Isolation After APEC
before.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces growing diplomatic isolation on the world stage following frosty exchanges with China at last week's APEC summit over her remarks on Taiwan. The cool reception has made it harder to envisage an end to year-long tensions amid Tokyo's concerns over Chinese military expansionism.

after.story: Japan's Takaichi Faces Diplomatic Isolation After APEC
after.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces diplomatic strain following icy exchanges with Chinese officials at the APEC summit in Shenzhen regarding Taiwan. Observers noted Beijing underscored its dissatisfaction by assigning a retired diplomat to meet Takaichi upon arrival.

before.story: CAS to Release Senegal AFCON Title Appeal Verdict
before.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced it will publish its verdict on Tuesday regarding Senegal's appeal over the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ten months after a chaotic final against Morocco.

after.story: CAS Reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON Champions on Appeal
after.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) officially ruled on Senegal's appeal, overturning the Confederation of African Football's prior decision to strip Senegal of their title. CAS declared Senegal the rightful 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions, stripping Morocco of the trophy ten months after the disputed final.

note: CAS officially grants Senegal's appeal, stripping Morocco and reinstating Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions.

before.story: Spain's Supreme Court Amnesties Carles Puigdemont
before.summary: Spain's Supreme Court applied the amnesty law to extinguish the criminal liability of former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont and former ministers Puig and Comín, formally closing the long-running 'Procés' independence case nearly a decade after it began.

after.story: Carles Puigdemont Sets December Return to Spain Following Supreme Court Amnesty
after.summary: Spain's Supreme Court applied the amnesty law to extinguish criminal liability for former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont and ministers Puig and Comín, officially closing the 'Procés' independence case. Following the dismissal, Puigdemont announced he will return to Barcelona on December 12, 2026, to unveil a renewed strategy for Catalan independence without asking for permission or forgiveness.

note: Puigdemont sets December 12, 2026 return to Barcelona after Supreme Court drops charges.

before.story: UK Government Welfare Review
before.summary: Former minister Alan Milburn proposed a radical welfare overhaul to support 440,000 NEETs by removing under-25s from sickness benefits, though ministers face conflicting recommendations regarding the protection of disability cash payments.

after.story: UK Government Welfare Review
after.summary: The UK government is attempting to reconcile two major welfare reviews: Alan Milburn's report recommending removing under-25s from sickness benefits to support 440,000 NEETs, and Sir Stephen Timms's disability benefits review. The Timms review rejects tougher eligibility rules for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), recommending faster payouts without mandatory reassessments for claimants with severe conditions despite warnings over a growing £40 billion welfare bill.

note: Timms review recommends faster PIP payments for severe conditions without mandatory reassessment.
